draft.title: Misleading and deceptive conduct
card: Misleading and deceptive conduct is when a business gives a false picture of what it sells, so buyers are tricked or left with the wrong idea. It is against the Australian Consumer Law.

Three common examples are false claims about a product, fake prices and hidden fees. A fake price is a "was" price that was never really charged. A hidden fee is a cost the buyer is not told about until late.
A business can break the rule even without a lie. Leaving out important facts, or a picture or wording that gives the wrong idea, can also mislead.
The ACCC (a national body) and Consumer Affairs Victoria (a Victorian body) enforce the rules. They can investigate businesses that break them.
draft.remember: A business must not give buyers a false picture, and the ACCC and Consumer Affairs Victoria enforce this.

a.q: A shop puts a "Was $100, now $60" sign on a jacket that was never sold for $100. Why is this a problem?
opts: It is a fake price that gives buyers a false picture
It is a hidden fee added after the buyer has paid
It is a faulty product that should be refunded
It is a sale that should have been approved first
a.why: The "was" price was never charged, so the sign makes the discount look bigger than it is. That gives buyers a false picture. A hidden fee is a different example, because it is about a cost buyers are not told about.
a.clue: Was the $100 price ever really charged?

b.q: Ravi's online store in Geelong advertises a game for $29. At checkout, a $12 "service fee" appears that was not mentioned before. Which statement best describes this?
opts: It may be misleading conduct, because of a hidden fee
It is fine, because the $29 price was true
It is a fake price, because the game is not worth $29
It is a major fault, so the buyer must get a refund
b.why: A cost the buyer is not told about until late is a hidden fee, and this can mislead buyers about the real price. The $29 being a true figure does not fix this, because leaving out important facts can also mislead. It is not a fake price, since that is about a "was" price never charged.
b.clue: A business can mislead without telling a lie.

a.best: It is a fake price that gives buyers a false picture

b.best: It may be misleading conduct, because of a hidden fee

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('may be'), while the wrong options make flat or absolute claims ('must get a refund', 'is fine'). A test-wise student could pick it on the qualifier alone without knowing the idea.
